parts.original_hypothesis: Root: P(churn) = sigmoid(-1.729 + linear_backbone + state_offsets + usage_service_nonlinear + minor_hinges), additive in logit; the four children never feed each other. 26 unconnected inputs (24 state one-hots, areaCode:510, totalEveCalls, totalEveCharge, totalIntlMinutes, totalIntlCalls and others) are zero-effect entries. Interpretation: a logistic-regression backbone (international plan +, voicemail plan -, intl charge +, night minutes +), a per-state offset table (exactly linear in the one-hots), and a block of genuine ReLU hinges on day/evening usage and customer-service calls that implements the known churn rules (heavy day usage without voicemail; 4+ service calls, especially with low day usage). Evidence (train, 4,000 rows): AUC 0.908, acc 0.909. Mean-ablation AUC: linear_backbone -> 0.826, usage_service_nonlinear -> 0.709, state_offsets -> 0.902, minor_hinges -> 0.908. Replacing every hidden unit by its least-squares linear fit on its own inputs gives AUC 0.836 (L2 logistic regression on all 71 inputs: 0.843), so essentially all of the gain over a linear model comes from usage_service_nonlinear (Shapley share: heavy usage/service tradeoff 0.029, service calls with low day usage 0.018, day charge without voicemail 0.016, service-call hinge 0.007, day-minutes hinge 0.002). Rare-category effects (net logit, train rows): state:11 -2.14 (73 rows, 3 churners; empirical log-odds offset -1.20), state:4 +2.02 (41 rows; empirical +0.83), state:47 +1.17 (72), state:26 +0.92 (75), state:0 -0.76 (56), state:22 suppresses the low-usage service-call unit (in-state effect -1.97 to +0.98). These are 1.5-2.5x the empirical offsets: candidates for repair. SHAP (300 rows) top: day charge, customer-service calls, international plan, voicemail plan, eve minutes, day minutes (the same column as day charge after z-scoring), intl charge, night minutes, vmail messages, account length.
variables: number of calls to customer service

parts.name: usage_service_nonlinear
parts.original_hypothesis: Additive sum (identity node nl_agg, weight 1) of the five leaves on the continuous usage and service-call inputs. The leaves never feed each other; they are summed in logit. Together they encode the classic churn rules: churn rises sharply with heavy day+evening usage (heavy_usage, day_charge_no_voicemail, day_minutes_hinge) and with 4+ customer-service calls (service_calls_hinge), especially when day usage is low (service_calls_low_day_usage), while heavy users are not penalised again for calls (10992). This block is where the network beats logistic regression: replacing each leaf by its least-squares linear fit on its own entry inputs lowers train AUC from 0.908 to 0.836 (L2 logistic regression on all 71 inputs: 0.843). Shapley split of that 0.072 AUC: heavy_usage_and_service_tradeoff 0.029, service_calls_low_day_usage 0.018, day_charge_no_voicemail 0.016, service_calls_hinge 0.007, day_minutes_hinge 0.002. Evidence (train, 4,000 rows): closed form from get_formula; viz summary attached; local mean-ablation of this part's logit contribution gives AUC 0.709 (baseline 0.908), logit SD 1.541; replacing it by its best linear fit on its inputs gives AUC 0.836.
variables: number of calls to customer service

parts.name: linear_backbone
parts.original_hypothesis: Sparse linear backbone: 34 inputs add weighted terms, summed at identity node lin_agg (read out by the output with weight 1). Output is P(churn). Largest z-scored weights: internationalPlan +0.77, voiceMailPlan -0.74, numberVmailMessages +0.42 (offsets part of the voiceMailPlan term; the two are almost collinear), totalIntlCharge +0.32, totalNightMinutes +0.24, totalDayCalls +0.11, accountLength +0.10. State one-hots are rare (about 80 rows each) so their z-scored value is about 8.5 and small weights become large offsets: state:11 -2.14 logit (73 rows, 3 churners), state:47 +1.17, state:26 +0.92, state:50 -0.64, state:21 +0.64, state:8 +2.35 (cancelled by unit 3831, see state8_offset). totalEveMinutes (+0.01) and totalNightCharge (-0.01) are negligible here. Evidence (train, 4,000 rows): closed form from get_formula (3 s.f. display matches exit activations to 0.00443); viz summary attached; local mean-ablation of this part's logit contribution gives AUC 0.826 (baseline 0.908), logit SD 1.094.

parts.name: heavy_usage_and_service_tradeoff
parts.original_hypothesis: Heavy-usage detector with a service-call bump that heavy usage switches off. 7701 = relu(1.23*dayCharge + 1.46*eveMinutes - 0.506); 5611 = relu(0.60*dayCharge + 0.69*7701 + 0.01*state:40 - 0.763) = relu(1.45*dayCharge + 1.01*eveMinutes - 1.11) when 7701 is on; readout +1.30. So churn rises steeply (about 1.9 logit per SD of day charge) once combined day+evening usage is high: 5611 is on for 27% of rows (churn 27% vs 9%); mean contribution +1.69 logit at 250-300 day minutes and +3.48 above 300. 10992 = relu(0.68*custServCalls - 1.48*5611 - 0.585), readout +1.22: extra churn from customer-service calls (on for 73-100% of rows with 3+ calls; +0.63 logit at 4 calls, +1.9 at 6), cancelled when 5611 is large (heavy users who call are not penalised again). The state:40 weight (0.01) is negligible. Note: after z-scoring, totalDayCharge and totalDayMinutes are the same column (charge is an exact multiple of minutes), so the network uses them interchangeably. Evidence (train, 4,000 rows): closed form from get_formula (3 s.f. display matches exit activations to 0.0121); viz summary attached; local mean-ablation of this part's logit contribution gives AUC 0.878 (baseline 0.908), logit SD 0.863; replacing it by its best linear fit on its inputs gives AUC 0.896.
variables: number of calls to customer service

parts.name: service_calls_low_day_usage
parts.original_hypothesis: 104 = relu(-0.71*dayMinutes + 0.54*custServCalls - 0.27*state:22 + 0.09*2546 - 0.489), readout +1.54: many customer-service calls AND low day usage -> churn (train: customers with 4+ calls and under 160 day minutes churn 88%, vs 26% at 160-250 minutes). Mean contribution +0.03 logit at 0 calls, +0.89 at 4, +2.6 at 6+. state:22 subtracts 0.27*7 = 1.9 from the pre-activation, so the unit is almost never on in state 22 (1.3% vs 29% of rows): a state-specific exception fitted to 80 rows. 2546 = relu(0.20*custServCalls + 0.28*4382 - 0.915) and 4382 = relu(0.28*dayCalls - 0.17*intlCharge - 0.48) are a nearly dead side chain (2546 on for 0.1% of rows, weight 0.09). Note: after z-scoring, totalDayCharge and totalDayMinutes are the same column (charge is an exact multiple of minutes), so the network uses them interchangeably. Evidence (train, 4,000 rows): closed form from get_formula (3 s.f. display matches exit activations to 0.00254); viz summary attached; local mean-ablation of this part's logit contribution gives AUC 0.893 (baseline 0.908), logit SD 0.595; replacing it by its best linear fit on its inputs gives AUC 0.904.

parts.name: day_charge_no_voicemail
parts.original_hypothesis: 10110 = relu(0.89*dayCharge - 0.95*vmailMessages - 0.801), readout +1.39: high day charge raises churn, but only for customers without voicemail messages. With 0 messages the hinge starts at about 0.29 SD of day charge (about $33.3, 196 minutes); each 13.5 messages pushes the threshold up by about 1 SD, so it is on for 38% of no-voicemail customers and 1% of the others. Mean contribution +1.30 logit at 250-300 day minutes, +2.36 above 300. Note: after z-scoring, totalDayCharge and totalDayMinutes are the same column (charge is an exact multiple of minutes), so the network uses them interchangeably. Evidence (train, 4,000 rows): closed form from get_formula (3 s.f. display matches exit activations to 0.00106); viz summary attached; local mean-ablation of this part's logit contribution gives AUC 0.896 (baseline 0.908), logit SD 0.545; replacing it by its best linear fit on its inputs gives AUC 0.903.

parts.name: state_offsets
parts.original_hypothesis: Additive sum (identity node state_agg, read out with weight 1) of the five state-only hidden leaves. Every unit here has only state one-hot inputs, and the categories are mutually exclusive, so the block is exactly a per-state logit offset table: state:4 +2.02 (41 rows), state:8 -2.31 (cancels the backbone's +2.35), state:0 -1.25, state:22 +0.98, state:42 +0.59, state:46 +0.02, state:29 0, plus a constant. Nominally nonlinear (ReLU) but functionally linear in the one-hots. Mean-ablating the block changes train AUC 0.908 -> 0.902. Evidence (train, 4,000 rows): closed form from get_formula; viz summary attached; local mean-ablation of this part's logit contribution gives AUC 0.902 (baseline 0.908), logit SD 0.443.

parts.name: state8_offset
parts.original_hypothesis: Unit 3831 = relu(0.40*s8 + 1.169) (always on) read out with -0.82: an offset of -2.31 logit in state:8 (81 rows) that almost exactly cancels the backbone's direct state:8 term (+2.35). Net state:8 effect +0.04 logit. A cancelling pair of large terms; exactly affine in the indicator. Evidence (train, 4,000 rows): closed form from get_formula (3 s.f. display matches exit activations to 0.000592); viz summary attached; local mean-ablation of this part's logit contribution gives AUC 0.904 (baseline 0.908), logit SD 0.325.

parts.name: service_calls_hinge
parts.original_hypothesis: 7420 = relu(0.58*custServCalls - 0.612), readout +1.23: a hinge that adds 0.55 logit per customer-service call above 3 calls (0.02 at 3, 0.56 at 4, 1.11 at 5, 1.65 at 6). parts.name: state4_state42_offset
parts.original_hypothesis: Units fed only by state:4 (41 rows) and state:42 (68 rows). 791 = relu(0.57*s4 + 0.32*s42 + 0.136) takes 3 values (the categories are exclusive); 11938 = relu(0.89*791 - 0.227) is on only in those two states; 3979 = relu(0.45*s4 - 1.212) is on only in state 4. parts.name: state0_state46_offset
parts.original_hypothesis: 10511 = relu(0.95*s0 - 0.02*s46 + 0.576) and 14444 = relu(1.00*s0 + 0.432), readouts -0.13 and -0.02. Exact offsets: state:0 -1.25 logit (56 rows), state:46 +0.02. parts.name: state22_offset
parts.original_hypothesis: Two units with the single input state:22 (80 train rows). 1508 = relu(1.709 - 1.39*s22) is on (1.91) outside state 22 and off inside it; read out with -0.55, it adds +0.98 logit inside state 22 relative to other states. 14933 = relu(0.98*s22 + 0.454) has readout -0.01 (negligible). Any function of one binary input is affine in it, so this leaf is exactly a per-category offset. (state:22 also gates service_calls_low_day_usage, a separate leaf.) Evidence (train, 4,000 rows): closed form from get_formula (3 s.f. display matches exit activations to 0.00304); viz summary attached; local mean-ablation of this part's logit contribution gives AUC 0.908 (baseline 0.908), logit SD 0.137.

parts.name: day_minutes_hinge_off_in_state37
parts.original_hypothesis: 14295 = relu(1.00*state:37 + 0.201) is 0.05 outside state 37 and 7.02 inside it (84 rows). 5071 = relu(0.25*dayMinutes + 0.01*state:0 - 0.25*14295 - 0.26), readout +0.96: a small extra hinge on day minutes above about 1 SD (on for 13% of rows; +0.13 logit at 250-300 minutes, +0.34 above 300), switched off in state 37 (-1.75 on the pre-activation). The direct 14295 readout (+0.03) gives state 37 a +0.21 logit offset. Minor: mean-ablation changes AUC by under 0.001. Note: after z-scoring, totalDayCharge and totalDayMinutes are the same column (charge is an exact multiple of minutes), so the network uses them interchangeably. Evidence (train, 4,000 rows): closed form from get_formula (3 s.f. display matches exit activations to 0.00183); viz summary attached; local mean-ablation of this part's logit contribution gives AUC 0.908 (baseline 0.908), logit SD 0.063; replacing it by its best linear fit on its inputs gives AUC 0.908.

parts.name: minor_hinges
parts.original_hypothesis: Three negligible single-input units read out directly by the output: 15584 = relu(0.99*accountLength - 0.687) (readout +0.11, on for 24% of rows), 14725 = relu(1.00*nightCalls - 0.275) (readout -0.04), 16351 = relu(1.00*areaCode:415 - 0.932) (value 0.06 in area 415, readout +0.0007). Together the logit SD is 0.044 and mean-ablation leaves train AUC unchanged (0.908). Evidence (train, 4,000 rows): closed form from get_formula (3 s.f. display matches exit activations to 0.00755); viz summary attached; local mean-ablation of this part's logit contribution gives AUC 0.908 (baseline 0.908), logit SD 0.044; replacing it by its best linear fit on its inputs gives AUC 0.908.

parts.name: state29_dead_unit
parts.original_hypothesis: Dead chain: 7983 = relu(-0.30*s29 - 1.068) is 0 on every row (both values of the indicator give a negative pre-activation), so 15835 = relu(7983 + 0.306) = 0.306 is a constant and its readout -0.15 is a constant -0.046 logit bias. state:29 has no effect. reference_patient.definition: the typical patient: the median training patient for every number and the most common training category for every category (not a real patient)

confidence_rules.clearly: a meaningful change in predicted risk for a typical patient (at least 5% points), the test split agrees (same sign, and its bootstrap interval over test patients excludes no benefit), and every group has at least 20 training patients
confidence_rules.consistently across patients: the claim holds for at least 90% of training patients (range across patients); this is not a significance statement
confidence_rules.on the training data only: the test split disagrees (opposite sign, or no benefit on test patients) or is unclear (its interval includes no benefit), or no test check is available
confidence_rules.slightly: the change in predicted risk for a typical patient is below 5% points
confidence_rules.the model has little data on this: a compared group has fewer than 20 training patients

settings.effect_scale: log-odds (output pre-activation) for verification; predicted risk for the typical patient for wording
